conclusions: No stable native speedup is demonstrated for the primary 100k/depth-two complete broad-search case: each cohort has only three of six faster wall-time pairs and a near-zero median paired wall reduction.

Small 1k/depth-two broad search and cached 100k/depth-two broad projection retain positive paired wall and CPU medians in both cohorts; these are the clearest favorable repeated native observations, limited to the measured workloads.
Flat broad projection and deep broad search reverse wall-time direction between cohorts. A secondary combined median does not erase either reversal.
Sparse/no-match/blank controls and broad-search cases vary. No blanket macOS, whole-player, typing-latency, or retained-memory speedup claim is supported.
The Linux allocation reduction and Linux component timing results remain independent evidence; native allocation behavior was not measured.
limits: Native artifact omits executable binaries and build caches. Recorded executable SHA256 values cannot be independently recomputed from this archive.

Local partial clone lacks the recorded merge object. Merge identity and parents, the merged recognizer, and the pinned original Filter were independently fetched from GitHub; other source inputs match the reviewed branch and the archived compiled bytes.

Native host is a virtual Apple M1 with no recorded CPU affinity; Linux is a pinned logical Xeon CPU with another compiler, runtime and locale. No cross-platform absolute timing or allocation extrapolation.
Large native cases calibrate to one operation per process. Six pairs have substantial host/run variance and are not individual UI latency percentiles.
All completed observations, including unfavorable and high-variance records, are retained. No outlier deletion or benchmark rerun was performed in this audit.

The combined estimate is secondary; separate cohort estimates and variation must remain visible. Twelve pairs on two virtual runner allocations are not a representative hardware sample or UI-latency distribution.

method.combined_formula: Median of all 12 within-run pair reductions for the same case. This is not the mean of cohort medians or the ratio of pooled marginal medians.
method.within_pair_formula: 100 * (1 - candidate_time / baseline_time), with identical iteration counts within each pair

scope: Secondary summary of exactly two native cohorts; all 12 within-run pairs per case retained. No benchmark or CI rerun performed by this audit.
